free_tier.stated: 100 GB for PS5 saves and 100 GB for PS4 saves, so 200 GB total, plus a hard limit of 1,000 PS4 save files. Requires an active PS Plus subscription

per_object_cap.stated: 1,000 PS4 save files; no per-file byte cap published

retention.stated: While the subscription is active. No retention clock published

egress.terms: Console-mediated only. There is no HTTP API, so there is no egress path at all

tooling: none documented. PS4 save decryption is a separate jailbreak scene and not a storage API
chaining: Not chainable. Even filled to 200 GB the bytes are opaque save blobs retrievable only by a PS5 or PS4, so there is no read path to build on

limits.value: uploads happen from the console UI and need a PSN-authenticated console

identity_cost.detail: a PSN account and a paid subscription

reliability_note: The read path is console-only, which is the upload-open and read-gated failure in its purest form: a write quota with no programmatic read is not storage

evidence.proved: every step is console UI, 'Settings > Saved Data and Game/App Settings > Upload to Cloud Storage'
'100 GB of online storage ... The number of PS4 saved data files you can store is limited to 1000'

price_per_tb_month: Bundled with PS Plus Essential at about USD 79.99/yr; 100 GB is not purchasable separately
binding_note: 200 GB on a paid subscription, but the gate that matters is that the only client is a console: there is no path to read the bytes from a server.

extras.cross_topic_note: the storage topic carries the same provider from the game-save angle
